_readme: Calibration sets (COLLECTION.md §4) for PRO-89. Both keys were registered
2026-09-07, BEFORE build-company-base.py ran and before any verdict or
entry_stage wrote. Every stage answer is anchored to an external document
-- the company's own press release, contemporaneous trade press, or the
issuer's Form D history -- never to Greylock's own site, because the
site's `firstPartnered` field is the LAYER UNDER TEST here.
Gate on membership: zero false members at high confidence.
Gate on stage: measured blind through the production protocol, then the
misses decomposed by layer (not by row) before the grind starts.

linkedin: Greylock led the $10M Series B, announced 2004-10-13 (news.linkedin.com/2004/10/linkedin-secures-10-million-in-series-b-funding-led-by-greylock); David Sze board seat to the 2016 Microsoft acquisition
facebook: Greylock and Meritech led the $27.5M round of April 2006; listed on every site era since
airbnb: Greylock led the $7.2M Series A, Nov 2010, Reid Hoffman board (finsmes.com/2010/11/airbnb-raises-7-2m-in-series-a-funding)
figma: Greylock led the $14M Series A, Dec 2015, John Lilly board (venturecapitaljournal.com/figma-scores-14-mln-series-a)
palo-alto-networks: Greylock wrote a $250K seed check in 2005; Nir Zuk worked from Greylock's offices, Asheem Chandna board (greylock.com/cybersecurity)
abnormal: Greylock led the $24M Series A, launched from stealth 2019-11-19 (abnormal.ai/newsroom/press-releases/launching-24m-series-a-funding-from-greylock); issuer's first Form D 2019-12-05
discord: Greylock led the ~$20M round of Jan 2016, Josh Elman board; the firm's own post 'Our Investment in Discord', 2016-01-27
cloudera: Greylock led the Series B, closed 2009-06-02 (cloudera.com press release); Accel led the A
mentor-graphics-corporation: 1981 start-up investment, IPO 1984 — the firm's own 1999 listing carries the year and the outcome
workday: Greylock led the first institutional round in 2005 alongside Dave Duffield; Aneel Bhusri co-founder and Greylock partner
ai-fund: TRAP, fund-shaped list entry (T5). Listed on greylock.com/portfolio with no entry round; AI Fund is Andrew Ng's venture studio and fund, not an operating company Greylock holds equity in as a venture position. The standing rule: a fund-shaped name that cannot be identified as an operating company is not_member until evidence identifies it otherwise
gofundme: TRAP, control position (T3, Erik 2026-09-04). June 2015: an investor group led by Accel and TCV, INCLUDING GREYLOCK, took a controlling stake by buying founders' shares at a ~$600M valuation (techcrunch.com/2015/06/24/gofundmes-investors-take-a-controlling-stake-in-latest-financing-round). A control acquisition is not a venture round; the row belongs in excluded.csv as control_position, not in the base. The site nonetheless labels it 'Series A'
greylock-xiv-limited-partnership: TRAP, the firm's own fund vehicle (T5). Appears in the EDGAR entity registry and must never become a portfolio row
83north-ii-limited-partnership: TRAP, separately advised affiliate (T1, decisions.md D3). 83North holds its own registrations (CRD 283471, 294729); its funds are not Greylock vehicles and its companies are not Greylock rows
greylock-israel-l-p: TRAP, own ERA (T1, decisions.md D2). GREYLOCK ISRAEL GLOBAL MANAGEMENT LTD. reports under CRD 162176 / SEC file 802-75092, separate from the home adviser's CRD 161537
siemens: TRAP, ACQUIRER MARK (the First Round lesson). Greylock's 2001-2003 and 2005-2010 listings carry outcome text such as 'Acquired by Siemens in 1999' beside the company; a name-matching layer reads the acquirer as a listed company
greylock-capital-management: TRAP, namesake firm (decisions.md D4/R1). Hans Humes' New York distressed-debt manager, CRD 137825, shares the word and nothing else; its Global / Emerging Markets / Distressed Debt funds are not Greylock Partners vehicles
conviction: TRAP, ex-partner next-firm deal (T4). Sarah Guo was a Greylock partner and left in 2022 to found Conviction; deals she has led since are Conviction's, and her name on a post-2022 Form D locates her at Conviction, not Greylock
robinhood: TRAP, personal and next-firm seat (T4). Josh Elman was a Greylock partner and later a Robinhood product VP; a Section 16 filing by him is a person-level filing and never a Greylock fund position. No Greylock fund is on Robinhood's cap table through a Greylock vehicle
check-point-software: TRAP, operator history not a position (T2/T4). Asheem Chandna was a Check Point executive before joining Greylock in 2003; the employer of a partner before their tenure is not a portfolio company
camp-greylock: TRAP, name collision (T5). A Massachusetts summer camp that shares the word and appears in web and job-board search results for the firm
workday-inc-401k: TRAP, scrape artifact (T5). Benefit-plan and filer-agent entities that carry a portfolio company's name are not rows

stage._key_registered: 2026-09-07, before entry_stage published anywhere. Answers are external documents; Greylock's own `firstPartnered` field is recorded beside each answer as the LAYER SCORE, not as the key. Taxonomy is the closed four: Pre-Seed | Seed | Series A | Growth, where Growth is Series B and later.
airbnb: Series A, $7.2M, Nov 2010, Greylock led with Sequoia, Reid Hoffman board (finsmes.com/2010/11/airbnb-raises-7-2m-in-series-a-funding)
figma: Series A, $14M, Dec 2015, Greylock led, $48.4M post; Index led the 2013 seed (venturecapitaljournal.com/figma-scores-14-mln-series-a)
palo-alto-networks: $250K seed check, 2005, Nir Zuk working from Greylock's offices; Sequoia alongside (greylock.com/cybersecurity)
workday: Greylock led the first institutional round in 2005 alongside the founder's own money; no prior priced round exists
okta: Series B, $16.5M, Aug 2011, Greylock and Khosla joining a16z and Floodgate; a16z led the 2010 Series A (techcrunch.com/2011/08/08/khosla-greylock-andreessen-horowitz-put-16-5m-in-enterprise-cloud-app-management-startup-okta)
nextdoor: First investment March 2012, then led the $21.6M round of Oct 2012 — Series B or later either way (greylock.com/blog/congrats-nextdoor)
discord: Greylock led the ~$20M round of Jan 2016 with Tencent, Benchmark and YouWeb, after the 2015 seed and Series A; Josh Elman board (globalventuring.com/blog/2016/02/02/tencent-fuels-discord-for-20m-round)
coinbase: Greylock's own announcement 'Our Investment in Coinbase', 2017-08-10, well after the 2013 Series A
cloudera: Series B, closed 2009-06-02, Greylock led; Accel led the March 2009 Series A (cloudera.com/about/news-and-blogs/press-releases/2009-06-02-cloudera-the-commercial-hadoop-company-closes-series-b-funding.html)
opendns: Greylock and Sequoia took the Series A in July 2009 (techcrunch.com/2009/07/07/sequoia-opendns-greylock)
appdynamics: Greylock co-led the $5.5M Series A with Lightspeed, announced 2008-04-04 — the company's first venture funding (appdynamics.de/newsroom/press-release/appdynamics-secures-55-million-venture-funding-greylock-ventures-and-lightspeed)
sumo-logic: Greylock led the $5.8M Series A in April 2010; Sutter Hill led the $15M Series B of Jan 2012 (techcrunch.com/2012/01/31/log-data-management-and-analytics-startup-sumo-logic-raises-15m-from-greylock-and-others)
abnormal: Greylock led the $24M Series A, launched from stealth 2019-11-19; the issuer's FIRST Form D is 2019-12-05, so no earlier priced round exists (abnormal.ai/newsroom/press-releases/launching-24m-series-a-funding-from-greylock)
cribl: Greylock co-led the $200M SERIES C with Redpoint, Aug 2021; CRV led both the 2019 seed and the 2020 Series A and Sequoia led the Series B (cribl.io/blog/greylock-redpoint-lead-cribl-series-c-200-million)
tellapart: Greylock led the $4.75M first round of financing, April 2010, James Slavet board; $4.75M is above the era's seed ceiling (techcrunch.com/2010/04/13/former-googlers-launch-tellapart-raise-4-75-million-from-greylock)
handshake: CORRECTED 2026-09-07, before the grind: the key row was written against the wrong company. Greylock's 'Handshake' is handshake.org, the decentralized naming and certificate-authority protocol (partner Mike Duboe), not Joinhandshake the campus-recruiting platform whose Series B Greylock led in 2016. The recognition check §3 asks for, applied late. Greylock's entry is the Series A of the protocol company, which is also what its own field says.

layer_scores._scored: 2026-09-07, before the grind, against the `stage` key above.

site_entry_stage.source: greylock.com Sanity portfolioCompany.firstPartnered (157 of 158 live rows carry it)
site_entry_stage.overall: 11/17 (12/17 after the handshake key was corrected)
site_entry_stage.verdict: SPLIT — class 1 for a Series B-or-later claim, DEMOTED to corroboration for Seed and Series A
diagnosis: The misses are one class, not seven rows. Where Greylock was the first
institutional money the field says 'Seed' whatever the record calls the
round: AppDynamics' $5.5M Series A (2008), Sumo Logic's $5.8M Series A
(2010), TellApart's $4.75M first round (2010) and Abnormal's $24M Series A
(2019) are all 'Seed' on the site, and Abnormal's first Form D is the
Series A itself, so no earlier priced round exists to rescue the label.
Cribl is the same field failing in the other direction and by two buckets:
'Seed' for a company Greylock entered at the $200M SERIES C in 2021, four
years and three leads after CRV's actual seed. Handshake is the Series A
claim failing the same way (Greylock led the 2016 Series B).
So the field is not a round name at all -- it is the firm's own sense of
how early it felt, and it is safe only in the direction where feeling
early is not the claim being made.
Consequence for the grind: 116 of 158 live rows (1 Pre-seed, 68 Seed,
47 Series A) carry a claim this gate refuses to publish, so entry_stage
for them comes from the record -- web citation first, then the issuer's
Form D position, then knowledge -- with the site field recorded as
corroboration only. Rows the site calls Series B or later publish from it.

Correction, same day: the 'handshake' key row was written against Joinhandshake, the campus-recruiting company, while Greylock's Handshake is handshake.org, the naming protocol. Scored again on the right company the Series A claim is 4/4, so the layer's failure is entirely in its Seed bucket and the demotion narrows to that claim — a golden label being wrong and corrected by the evidence, which §4 says the scoring must allow in both directions.

announcement_archive.source: greylock.com/blog, the Sanity `post` type (207 posts, 2015-05 to 2026-07)
announcement_archive.verdict: REFUSED for entry_stage — it does not name rounds at all
diagnosis: Creandum's finding was that a firm's announcement archive scores as a
class-1 entry-stage layer; Menlo's was that it inverts on a firm that
leads later rounds into companies it seeded quietly. Greylock is a third
case: the archive is a THESIS archive. 'Our Investment in Rubrik',
'Our Investment in Discord' and 'Our Investment in Coinbase' were read in
full and none of them names a round or an amount. Only ~14 of the 207
posts are investment announcements, and the archive begins in 2015, so it
reaches neither the round word nor the book. It stays in the evidence
pack as a dated first-party record that the firm invested, which is
membership evidence and a first_seen ceiling, and nothing more.

archive_cards_invest_year.source: the firm's own YEAR FUNDED / investment-year column in the 1999-2001, 2001-2003 and 2005-2010 listings, parsed into sources/site/archive-cards.json
archive_cards_invest_year.verdict: class 1 for first_seen, unscored for entry_stage (it carries no round word)
diagnosis: 249 of 250 companies parsed so far carry the firm's own year, back to
1967. Read as a CLOSE year on the Menlo rule, never as an announcement
date. It is the only dated evidence that exists for the pre-window book,
where no Form D layer reaches.
